searchText: When OFFERing ephemeral headers, only bridges are expected to offer the 8 headers worth of padded depth (i.e. most recent header + 8 previous ones), right? As an individual node, I can just offer whatever list of headers I get when I accept an offer for the most recent set of headers, right? So say I am OFFERed only a single header (i.e. most recent header) and it matches with my current head as known from the Beacon network, I'm okay to only offer 1 ephemeral header to other peers, right? If a node is offered x -> x - 1 -> x - 2 -> ... x - y And a node accepts an anchor lets say `x - 2`, the node accepting should re-gossip `x-2 to x - y` - `x` is the latest header the bridge is aware of - `x - 2` is the latest head you are aware and is anchored via your oracle You have to regossip the whole range `x-2 to x - y` even if you only accept a subsection of that range. `x-2` is the anchor in this case, but the anchor you choose could have been anything in this case you would be offered 9 headers, you already have 8 and there is 1 new one, you would only accept the new one, you would then regossip all 9 I would agree with tihs being the expected/default behaviour. But is there anything agains node gossiping `from x-2 to x-y-2`? (basically the same number of blocks that it was offered) We already have a padding for redundency why would we need an even bigger padding? I'm not saying we _need_ it. I'm asking if it would be bad if we would do it? And why we would do it, specifically because we stripped some redundancy from the initial offer by not accepting it Either way, I'm fine with whatever, I don't have strong preference. I don't think it would be bad per se just not needed as this isn't a mechanism for backfilling, but the utility of the padding if I understand it was if there was momentary outages on a node for some reason. Ah, so this +8 padding is in every case? That is, also just a single block update? I had not interpreted the text like that before, but I can see that now. I guess it makes sense, normally nodes would not accept all those anyhow. "So normally this would be 1 header, unless a re-org occurred where multiple would be included. An additional 8 header's content keys, MUST be included in the Offer message as padding." This sentence made me originally interpret it as minimum 8 additional headers when a re-org occurred. It is more so `1 + re-org-depth + 8` So most of the time the re-org-depth would be 0 Ah, I see.

excerpts.author: kolbyml
excerpts.content:
If a node is offered

x -> x - 1 -> x - 2 -> ... x - y

And a node accepts an anchor lets say `x - 2`, the node accepting should re-gossip `x-2 to x - y`

- `x` is the latest header the bridge is aware of
- `x - 2` is the latest head you are aware and is anchored via your oracle

excerpts.author: kolbyml
excerpts.content: You have to regossip the whole range `x-2 to x - y` even if you only accept a subsection of that range. `x-2` is the anchor in this case, but the anchor you choose could have been anything

excerpts.author: kolbyml
excerpts.content: in this case  you would be offered 9 headers, you already have 8 and there is 1 new one, you would only accept the new one, you would then regossip all 9
